verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_filter_blocks_xss: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names run through the main logic: `parse_tag` uses `j, k, p, q, r, n`, `sanitize` uses `s, i, m`, and `normalize`/`bad_url` use `v`. The policy constants are well named and there are some docstrings, but the parser's index juggling is hard to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `sanitize()` is one function of about 100 lines that mixes comment handling, tag dispatch, meta/link special cases, attribute rebuilding and raw-text handling. `parse_tag` is about 55 lines. `find_close` and the comment regexes are recompiled on every call.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: An unterminated tag hits `break`, and an unclosed `<script>`/`<iframe>` also silently drops the rest of the document. There are magic constants (`0x20`, `0x110000`, `i + 5`, `i + 6`). On the plus side, the file is read and written with explicit utf-8/surrogateescape handling.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: General rules are in place: lowercased `on*` names, a `normalize()` that decodes entities and strips control characters, scheme checks, and meta refresh, srcdoc and SVG animate handling. But `<template>` and `<math>` are not specifically handled, textarea/title content is kept raw, and the hidden `test_filter_blocks_xss` failed.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Tags are rebuilt from the original spans, so quoting and whitespace are preserved. However, any dangerous pattern in a `<style>` block empties the whole block, unclosed or unterminated tags truncate the document, and the hidden `test_clean_html_unchanged` failed.
